# Attachment Endpoint Plan

Defines the attachment-side plan for linking an existing initialized parent document back into the executing document, including when that document is a nested instruction. Planning produces contract contributions; it does not itself establish a parent link.

## Configuration and planning

`plan` reads `spec` from `/clauseRuntime/work/candidate/<clauseKey>/parameters`, using the `clauseKey` constant. The relevant parameters are:

- `relationship`: only the exact value `cross-embedded` produces contributions. Other values produce an empty `contracts` object.
- `linkBy`: the channel assigned to the generated `attachDocument` operation.
- `parentOrigin`: the required identity of the parent’s initialized original document.
- `authority`: the party role that must appear in both parent and attachment rosters.

No defaults for these parameters are defined here. For `cross-embedded`, the plan contributes `embedded`, a Process Embedded contract targeting `/sources/parent`, and `attachDocument`, a Sequential Workflow Operation that calls `linkParent` with `call/request` and the captured `spec`. The returned plan always has `reads: []` and `states: {}`; it supplies no initial state values.

`validateConfiguration` returns `allowed: true` with an empty `code` without inspecting configuration. This is not confirmation that a link request will pass execution checks. `validateTransition` always rejects with `ATTACHMENT_POLICY_IMMUTABLE`.

## Linking requirements

The `attachDocument` request contains `document`: the exact publication of an existing initialized document, supplied as a Blue ID reference.

Execution requires `call/requireExactDocumentVersion` to be exactly `true`, otherwise it rejects with `ATTACHMENT_EXACT_REVIEW_REQUIRED`. If the executing document has `/activation`, it must be active, pass participant-access checks, and recognize `call/channel` as a party role or a currently listed representative channel named `role__repId`. These activation checks are conditional on `/activation` existing; the operation’s presence does not grant permission to a viewer.

Participant-access checks examine party and representative transports. External Channel values bypass the Timeline Access lookup. Other transports must be Timeline Channels: each must match a Timeline Access document at an activation `accessPaths` entry, with the same provider, the target timeline, and at least one allowed key from every required reader group. A single matching access document must satisfy those requirements for that transport.

`linkParent` also requires:

- `relationship` to remain `cross-embedded`, otherwise `ATTACHMENT_RETURN_LINK_NOT_NEEDED`.
- The supplied parent to contain `/contracts/initialized/document`, whose identity equals `parentOrigin`; missing initialization or a different origin is rejected.
- The supplied parent’s `/activation/active` to be exactly `true`.
- A nonempty parent `/activation/parties` roster. Every parent role must exist in the executing document’s `/activation/parties`, with an identical `lead/channel` identity and identical, nonempty, duplicate-free `readerKeys` sets. Key order is immaterial. `authority` must exist in both rosters, and no additional child role is permitted.

## Effects and outcomes

After all checks, an existing `/sources/parent` with the configured initialized origin returns `outcome: duplicate` without changing the stored publication. A different origin rejects with `ATTACHMENT_REPLACEMENT_FORBIDDEN`; the operation does not replace that link.

For a new link, execution appends changes adding the supplied publication’s Blue ID reference at `/sources/parent` and `{parentOrigin: ...}` at `/attachmentLink`, then returns `outcome: acceptedNew`. These paths belong to the executing document. A request or generated plan alone is not a confirmed link; the changes must belong to completed execution.

The supplied evidence omits the full Contracts execution specification, so additional runtime admission and completion rules are not established here.
